name: Nanjing
meta_description: TDSC investigative consulting in matters touching Nanjing: Jiangsu supplier and partner diligence, IP and trade secret concerns, and arbitration support.
hero_lede: Nanjing is the capital of Jiangsu Province and a centre for software, integrated circuits, petrochemicals, vehicles and biomedicine. Investigative work connected to the city usually concerns manufacturing partners, technology and trade secrets, and disputes before Jiangsu courts or the city's arbitration institutions.
intro: Nanjing is the capital of Jiangsu, one of China's largest provincial economies, and the main city of the western Yangtze River Delta. The Nanjing Municipal Bureau of Statistics reported 9.577 million permanent residents at the end of 2024 and regional GDP of about 1.85 trillion yuan, with services making up two thirds of output. The city is known for software, and also for integrated circuits, electronics, petrochemicals, steel, vehicle manufacturing, smart grid equipment and biomedicine. Its development zones, including the state-level Jiangbei New Area and the Nanjing and Jiangning economic and technological development zones, host many foreign-invested manufacturers, and its Yangtze port handled 3.71 million TEUs in 2024.

Organisations commission investigative work connected to Nanjing mainly because of its role in manufacturing and technology supply chains. Foreign companies with joint ventures, contract manufacturers or research partners in the city need to understand who they are dealing with, how a partner is connected to other businesses, and whether there are signs of diversion of business, intellectual property leakage or undisclosed related-party dealings. Buyers and investors review Jiangsu suppliers before contracting or acquiring. Disputes may be heard in Nanjing courts, including the Nanjing International Commercial Court and Nanjing Maritime Court, or in arbitration, and parties need lawful background and asset information to support them.

matters.title: Contract manufacturer and supplier verification
matters.text: Confirming that a Nanjing or wider Jiangsu supplier is what it claims to be, using public enterprise credit information, court and enforcement records available online, customs and certification data, and open sources, and identifying shareholders, legal representatives and related entities that may compete with or trade around the client.

matters.title: Trade secret and IP leakage concerns
matters.text: Supporting companies and their counsel where technology, designs or customer information may have left a Nanjing joint venture or research partner, by mapping new companies set up by former staff or partners, their filings, patents and trademarks, and their commercial links, within the limits of Chinese law.

matters.title: Joint venture partner reviews
matters.text: Reviewing a Jiangsu joint venture partner's corporate history, state or local government shareholders, litigation and enforcement record, and reputation ahead of a new venture, restructuring or exit, so that the client understands the partner's interests and leverage before negotiation or dispute.

matters.title: Petrochemical and industrial counterparties
matters.text: Researching counterparties in Nanjing's chemical, steel and heavy industry sectors for lenders, traders and investors, including environmental and safety enforcement history, regulatory penalties, ownership changes and the financial strain that can precede default or disputed supply contracts.

matters.title: Support for Nanjing proceedings
matters.text: Assisting counsel in cases before the Nanjing International Commercial Court, Nanjing Maritime Court or Nanjing arbitration institutions with background on opposing parties and witnesses and with identification of corporate interests, so that claims, interim measures and enforcement are assessed on documented information.

local_context.title: Nanjing International Commercial Court
local_context.text: Approved by the Supreme People's Court and unveiled in April 2023, the Nanjing International Commercial Court hears international commercial disputes below 5 billion yuan. Nanjing was the third city in Jiangsu to establish such a court, after Suzhou and Wuxi. Its creation reflects the volume of foreign-related trade and investment disputes in the province, and it is a likely forum for disputes involving foreign parties and Nanjing companies.

local_context.title: Nanjing Maritime Court
local_context.text: The Nanjing Maritime Court was established on 4 December 2019 and operates dispatched tribunals in Lianyungang, Nantong, Taizhou and Suzhou. It handles maritime and shipping cases arising along Jiangsu's coast and Yangtze waterways, including foreign-related disputes and ship arrest applications, and has signed cooperation arrangements with the China Maritime Arbitration Commission. It matters for shipping, cargo and trade finance disputes involving Nanjing and Jiangsu ports.

local_context.title: Arbitration in Nanjing
local_context.text: The Nanjing Arbitration Commission handles commercial arbitration in the city, and the Jiangsu (Nanjing) International Commercial Arbitration Centre opened there on 31 December 2020. The centre focuses on international trade, cross-border investment, mergers and acquisitions, finance, information technology, high-end manufacturing and shipping disputes. Parties choosing Nanjing arbitration often need research on counterparties and assets to evaluate claims, security and enforcement options.

local_context.title: Provincial courts and regulators
local_context.text: The Jiangsu High People's Court sits in Nanjing and hears appeals and major cases from across the province; it has published typical foreign-related commercial and maritime cases that indicate how Jiangsu courts approach such disputes. Provincial branches of national regulators, including market regulation and financial supervision bodies, are also based in the city, and their published penalties are useful in counterparty research.

local_context.title: Business registration and development zones
local_context.text: Nanjing had 1.818 million registered business entities in 2024, with 201,800 newly registered. Companies register with local market regulation authorities, and basic registration data appears in the national enterprise credit information publicity system. Development zone administrations, such as the Jiangbei New Area and Jiangning zones, publish investment announcements that help confirm a counterparty's projects, investment history and stated operating scale.

tdsc_approach: TDSC handles Nanjing matters from Nashville and has no office, staff or licence in China. Each engagement starts with a jurisdictional review, because Chinese law restricts the collection and export of personal information and certain data, and the authorities have scrutinised due diligence and consulting activity in recent years. TDSC works from lawfully accessible public records, published court and regulatory information, company disclosures and open sources, and does not commission surveillance, pretext enquiries or approaches to officials in China. Where a matter needs local work, it is scoped with PRC counsel. Reports are written so the client can see the sources, gaps and confidence of each conclusion.

faqs.q: What can be learned about a Nanjing company from public records?
faqs.a: Public enterprise registration data generally shows the company's name, registered capital, legal representative, shareholders as registered, business scope and administrative penalties. Court judgments and enforcement records are partly available online. These sources do not always show who ultimately controls a business, so conclusions on control are drawn carefully and labelled as such.

faqs.q: Can TDSC investigate a suspected trade secret leak in Nanjing?
faqs.a: TDSC can map the corporate and commercial footprint of former staff, partners and new competitors through lawful documentary sources, including registrations, patents, trademarks and litigation, and support PRC counsel preparing a claim. It does not carry out surveillance, covert approaches or collection of personal data in China that would breach Chinese law.

faqs.q: When might the Nanjing International Commercial Court be relevant?
faqs.a: It hears international commercial disputes below 5 billion yuan and was unveiled in April 2023 with Supreme People's Court approval. Where a contract with a Nanjing company leads to litigation in China rather than arbitration, counsel may consider it. TDSC supports such proceedings with background research on parties and assets.

faqs.q: Is Nanjing a seat for international arbitration?
faqs.a: Yes. The Nanjing Arbitration Commission operates in the city and the Jiangsu (Nanjing) International Commercial Arbitration Centre opened at the end of 2020, focusing on trade, investment, finance, technology, manufacturing and shipping disputes. Whether to choose it over other Chinese or overseas institutions is a question for counsel.

faqs.q: Why does sector matter in Nanjing supplier reviews?
faqs.a: Nanjing combines high-technology industries, such as software and integrated circuits, with petrochemicals, steel and heavy manufacturing. The relevant risks differ: technology leakage and related-party competition in the former, environmental and safety enforcement and financial strain in the latter. Reviews are scoped to the sector, the product and the client's exposure.
